svg.title: The rendezvous point in PIM-SM: a meeting place, a register handler and a state centre, and what survives when it fails
svg.desc: Top: a source reaches its first-hop router, which encapsulates traffic in Register messages to the RP; receivers join the shared tree toward the RP; the RP joins the source tree and stops the register. Bottom left: what still works after the RP dies - established (S,G) shortest path trees keep forwarding, existing receivers keep watching. Bottom right: what breaks - no new (*,G) join can complete, so new receivers see nothing, no new source can register, so new channels never open, and any RP-dependent monitoring goes blind.
svg.text: The RP is not a router in the path. It is the place where senders and receivers meet.
Three jobs, one address: rendezvous, register de-encapsulation, and source state that other PEs learn through MSDP.
S
FHR
RP
LHR
R
multicast stream
Register (unicast, PIM-encapsulated)
join the source tree, then Register-Stop
shared tree
Receivers join (*,G) toward the RP,
never toward the source. That is the
whole reason the RP exists.
Second job: de-encapsulate. The register carries real traffic until the RP has pulled the source tree, then Register-Stop ends the encapsulation.
Third job: hold the source state other RPs must learn about, which is why Anycast-RP needs MSDP and a single RP does not.
SURVIVES AN RP FAILURE
Anything already on a source tree
(S,G) state built by SPT switchover keeps forwarding
without any RP involvement. Existing viewers keep watching.
Anything already registered
The source is flowing, the FHR was told to stop registering,
and no RP is needed for that path to stay up.
This is exactly why an RP outage looks partial, not total.
BREAKS THE MOMENT THE RP DIES
New receivers cannot complete a join
(*,G) join travels toward an unreachable RP. A channel that
was working stays up; a channel nobody is watching cannot be opened.
New sources cannot register
No register means no first packet at the RP, so a new channel
stays black even though the sender is transmitting perfectly.
One RP, no redundancy: this is a permanent outage for new sessions, not a slow one.
Design consequence
If the business cannot accept "new channels fail", the RP needs Anycast-RP with MSDP or Phantom RP - and the failover budget must be written down, not assumed.
